approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic molecular optimizer with a Bayesian re-ranking layer in front of the oracle. It keeps every scored molecule of the current objective in a chronological archive and a bounded population of the sixty-four best. Each round it draws breeding parents from high-scoring quantiles of that population and builds a surplus pool of one hundred and sixty fresh de novo offspring, either by connected-fragment crossover of two parents with an optional finishing mutation, or by one to several successive graph edits of a single parent; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is switched off, offspring are admitted on stable canonical identity with duplicates rejected, and a narrow sulfur rule rejects any offspring that introduces an unusual sulfur environment its own breeding parents did not already carry. Before every batch a Gaussian process is refitted on the whole accepted archive: each molecule is represented by integer counts of hashed radius-two local environments, similarity between two molecules is the dot-product count Tanimoto of those counts, the observation noise is fixed and the scores are standardized by the current archive mean and spread. Ten molecules are then chosen from the pool by correlated posterior sampling - one joint draw of a function over the whole pool, take its maximum, mask it, repeat - so the batch follows sampled function values rather than predicted means.
approach.novelty: This Child gives the same Gaussian process a second, whole-molecule view of each candidate, and lets the task's own labels decide how much that view counts. Besides its local-environment counts, every molecule gets a fixed seventeen-number composition and property profile: heavy-atom count, per-element atom counts with the rare elements pooled, hydrogen count, ring and aromatic-ring counts, hydrogen-bond donors, hydrogen-bond acceptors, rotatable bonds, computed lipophilicity and polar surface area, each standardized against the current archive, compared through a Gaussian similarity. The covariance becomes a weighted blend of the two views, and at every refit the blend weight and the profile lengthscale are chosen from a small frozen grid by the exact marginal likelihood of the labels already in the archive. Zero weight is a grid point, so the Parent's own kernel stays selectable at every single fit and is used unchanged whenever the data prefer it. That is the difference from what the siblings tried: earlier covariance experiments on this Parent swapped one fixed law for another over the same local-environment counts, or averaged in a second structural channel at a forced equal weight, and every one of them lost endpoint score. Here the added channel describes the molecule as a whole rather than its fragments, and its influence is fitted rather than asserted. The three concurrent siblings change the local-environment radius, the number of fresh offspring ranked, or remove a mutation route; none of them changes what kind of information the model's similarity carries.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's surrogate knows a molecule only as a bag of hashed radius-two local environments. Its complete matched panel is macro mean 0.59645311428869 with population SD 0.03397032998399878 (seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287, 0.583088384937917; per-task means zaleplon 0.456810, deco_hop 0.706940, drd2 0.991017, median_2 0.222732, sitagliptin 0.604768 with task SDs 0.080095 and 0.105952 on the two widest streams). All fifteen sessions completed with 300 oracle calls each and no invalid or duplicate attempt (n-1744a1494180 seed summaries and run logs). Its own chronological receipts show the predictive limit is uneven rather than absent: the final selected-stream prediction MSE divided by the archive-mean MSE is 0.699/0.719/0.692 on sitagliptin and 0.360/0.489/0.467 on zaleplon across seeds 0/1/2, against 0.306/0.221/0.163 on deco_hop, 0.146/0.241/0.114 on drd2 and 0.214/0.275/0.077 on median_2. The two streams where local-environment similarity explains least of the label variation are also the two lowest non-degenerate task means. Pool uncertainty is not the obstacle: averaged over all 435 recorded pools only 2.0 to 3.9 percent of candidates sit above 0.9 of the prior marginal SD, so the model is confident and still wrong on those streams. A read-only replay of the registered grid over the Parent's own 435 recorded fit states (no oracle calls, no source change) selects a positive composition weight at 432 of them, and on the molecules the Parent actually evaluated next from the identical archive, the composite posterior mean lowers same-label MSE from 0.011213 to 0.006466 and raises mean within-batch Spearman from 0.5255 to 0.6675, with the largest movement on sitagliptin (0.4044/0.3950/0.4011 to 0.7710/0.7556/0.7677). Prior work on this Parent constrains the response rather than the diagnosis: every fixed unfitted substitution of the covariance law over the same folded count vocabulary lost endpoint mean (squared -0.044472 in n-36a7bb9883ec, exponential mean-only -0.058269 in n-14a52e3f8725, residual-only -0.029710 in n-6ebafca203bf, coherent exponential -0.033172 in n-a11bce06c3f9, normalized inner product -0.077227 in n-52bd6c308406), and the lesson recording that exhaustion explicitly scopes itself to fixed unfitted laws over the unchanged count vocabulary, leaving fitted kernel parameters and other molecular representations untested on this Parent. Forcing a second structural channel at equal weight also lost 0.033408 on the previous Parent (n-e75f0f495f9b), while adding genuinely richer predictive information under a retained kernel principle gained 0.022573 (n-559d25e9c9c7), and adding posterior selection at all gained 0.055880 (n-fc2c108a5253).
hypothesis: Replace the single fixed dot-product count-Tanimoto GP covariance with one per-fit exact-marginal-likelihood-selected convex blend K=(1-w)*T_DP+w*K_comp over the frozen grid w in {0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5} by squared lengthscale in {17/4, 17}, where K_comp is a Gaussian kernel on a fixed seventeen-feature archive-standardized whole-molecule composition/property vector and w=0 reproduces the inherited kernel exactly, then use that one selected kernel coherently in every training, cross, pool and probe Gram block for both the posterior mean and the correlated residual covariance.

finding_summary.headline: Composition channel ran exactly and improved ranking, but steered search toward larger molecules and lost 0.013 overall, mostly on deco_hop
finding_summary.insights:
Fitting the weight, rather than forcing it as the earlier equal-weight atom-pair channel did, shows that the labels clearly prefer a whole-molecule composition and property view. It does make the surrogate better on objectives that depend on global properties. But this is the fourth time in this lineage that better ranking of the tested molecules has failed to produce better endpoints. Marginal likelihood selects a kernel that fits the archive, not one that searches well, and that gap is now a pattern rather than an anecdote.

The failure has a specific, traceable route. A stationary Gaussian kernel on archive-standardized descriptors gives every compositionally novel molecule fresh prior variance. Under Thompson sampling that variance becomes a novelty bonus that scales with size, and the generator can grow molecules cheaply by appending atoms. Where the score band is narrow (deco_hop sits in 0.5 to 0.62), variance dominates the draw. The search then drifts toward big, repetitive molecules that the molecular review shows are not where the score is. This rules out implementation error, grid failure or numerical fallback as explanations.

The weight sat at the 0.5 grid edge on three tasks. Larger weights are untested, but given this mechanism they would more likely amplify the drift than fix it. The more informative next step is to separate the two roles: use the composition channel for the posterior mean and keep the Parent's local kernel for the sampled uncertainty, or otherwise stop composition novelty from earning exploration credit.

Still open: whether the small zaleplon and sitagliptin gains are real, given mixed seed signs and only three seeds. Also open: how much of the deco_hop loss is the Parent's one lucky late breakthrough rather than the size drift. All three deco_hop seeds and their areas under the curve are lower, which suggests the drift matters, but the attribution is associative. Among the four same-round variants on this Parent, all lost, and this was the smallest loss; those are dependent comparisons, not a ranking of ideas.
finding_summary.results:
The likelihood wanted the new whole-molecule view almost everywhere: 431 of 435 refits gave it positive weight, and 304 picked the largest weight on the grid (0.5). Only four early refits, with 20 to 30 molecules in the archive, kept the Parent's kernel. The preference grew as the archive grew and was strongest on sitagliptin and zaleplon. Every refit and every batch reproduced exactly when recomputed independently. Breeding and random draws were untouched: the first batch's candidate pool and random numbers match the Parent's in all 15 sessions.

On the molecules it actually tested, the blended model predicted better than the Parent's kernel would have from the same state. Error fell by about a quarter (0.0077 to 0.0058). Within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.43 to 0.54, and pairwise order accuracy from 0.67 to 0.71. Most of the gain came where the Parent's model was weakest: sitagliptin rank correlation went from about 0.18 to 0.48, and zaleplon from 0.43 to 0.59. deco_hop and median_2 barely moved, and median_2 error rose slightly in all three seeds. The improvement is about half the size the pre-registered replay suggested.

It also changed which molecules got tested. Against the Parent's kernel on the identical pool and draws, it swapped about half of each batch in 428 of 435 batches. It picked larger molecules in 14 of 15 sessions (+2.3 heavy atoms on average, +5 to +7 on deco_hop), and its batches were more self-similar in 14 of 15. The size pull comes from uncertainty, not from predicted score: the blend adds extra posterior spread to molecules at the edge of the archive's composition range, and that extra spread rises with molecule size in every session (rank correlation 0.31 to 0.65).

Scores: the complete matched mean was 0.5834 against the Parent's 0.5965, a change of -0.0131, well short of the +0.002 goal. Seed changes were -0.045, +0.008 and -0.002, and only 5 of 15 task/seed cells improved. deco_hop fell on all three seeds (task mean -0.096). That includes missing the Parent's late 0.856 breakthrough on seed 0, which by itself costs 0.016 of the mean; the other 14 cells net +0.003. On deco_hop the Child's tested molecules averaged roughly 48 heavy atoms against the Parent's 32, reaching 71 in the last third of one session, while the best deco_hop molecules have about 28; oracle time rose 7 to 36 fold. zaleplon (+0.014), sitagliptin (+0.012) and median_2 (+0.005) rose slightly, but the sign differed between seeds. drd2 finished level but progressed more slowly early (area under the curve -0.042). The Child produced more offspring that beat their own parents (860 against 648) and more new incumbents (325 against 255), yet final scores were not higher.

molecular.headline: Flat halogen-decorated heteroaromatics; the top of two objectives is held by O-F and N-F bonds, and no proposal carries stereochemistry or charge.
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child trajectory files named in the brief were present and read (3 seeds x 5 objectives, 300 evaluations each, 290 optimizer proposals per session, 870 per objective, 4350 in total; the digest reports 876-880 unique molecules per objective and tasks_without_trajectories is empty). Every one of the 4350 optimizer SMILES parses as a valence-legal structure. The output is ring-dense and flat: digest ring_closure_rate 0.978-0.999 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.920-0.997 across the five objectives, and by RDKit the mean molecule carries 2.6-6.3 rings of which 2.1-5.9 are aromatic, with mean fraction sp3 carbon only 0.17-0.37. Three absences are uniform and countable. Not one of the 4350 proposals carries a stereo designation, although 2282 of them (52.5%) contain at least one unassigned stereocentre. Not one carries a formal charge, although 796 of the 870 proposals on one objective carry a basic amine. And ordinary carbon-bound electron-withdrawing groups are almost unreachable: trifluoromethyl appears in 2 of 4350 molecules, nitrile in 11, tetrazole in 0, sulfonyl in 213 (almost all inherited from one seeded starting molecule), carboxylic acid in 87. What the generator does instead is decorate: digest halogen_rate is 0.883-0.994 on four of the five objectives, and 1179 of 4350 proposals (27.1%) place that halogen on a heteroatom rather than on carbon. Saturated heterocycles that a medicinal chemist would reach for first are nearly absent (morpholine in 2 proposals, an unfused piperazine ring in 15, piperidine in 114 of 4350), while strained three- and four-membered rings and bridges thrown across existing aromatic systems appear preferentially among the leaders. Against the Parent on the same three seeds (context.comparison: child_complete and paired_complete, matched seeds 0, 1, 2, paired_mean_delta -0.0131), the Child's molecules are larger (mean 33.4 versus 28.4 heavy atoms over all 4350) and this inflation is concentrated where the Child lost most: on one objective the Child averages 47.9 heavy atoms and 697 Da against the Parent's 31.8 and 472 Da, 32.6% of its proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms against the Parent's 2.3%, and in one session mean size climbs monotonically from 44.8 to 70.6 heavy atoms across the five fifths of the budget while the Parent's stays flat at 31.4 to 35.6. Citations below are drawn only from the digest and the Child staging trajectories named in context.citation_trajectory_paths; the Parent trajectories were read for comparison but are quoted only as aggregate numbers, never as SMILES.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-sized flat heteroaromatic amides: mean 24.8 heavy atoms, 376 Da, 3.45 rings of which 2.69 are aromatic, 4.0 rotatable bonds, cLogP 4.34, TPSA 61, QED 0.57, SA score 3.44 over the 870 proposals. The recurring body is an indole- or pyrrolo-fused 2-carboxamide capped by an N-aryl or N-pyridyl amide: amide in 82.6% of proposals, N-aryl nitrogen in 85.6%, aromatic ring nitrogen in 84.6%, aryl halide in 78.9%. Decoration is methyl, ethyl, methoxy and one halogen; there is no basic amine (14 of 870), no nitrile (1 of 870), no sulfonyl and no carboxylic acid anywhere. Scores run from 0.0 to 0.5129 with digest median 0.3488.
liabilities: benzylic bromide in 23.3% of the top 30 (CBr on the fused arene), a directly alkylating group placed on the scoring scaffold
bridged polycyclic cages spanning an aromatic ring in 90% of the top 30, which is where SA score rises to 4.71
hypobromite-type O-Br and other heteroatom-halogen bonds in 49 of 870 proposals
hydrazide and N-amino amide motifs in 14.7% of proposals, including the final-evaluation molecules
one- and two-atom fragments still proposed as candidates (1.1% of proposals below 10 heavy atoms)
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere (1 of 870 proposals), so the one strongly electron-withdrawing aromatic substituent the leaders never gain is the one their own scaffold class usually carries
no trifluoromethyl in any of the 870 proposals, leaving single-atom halogen as the only electronic tuning move
no basic amine centre (14 of 870) and no saturated N-heterocycle (0 piperidine, 0 piperazine, 0 morpholine)
no specified stereochemistry on any proposal, while the bridged leaders each introduce 1-2 unassigned centres
no simple acyclic N-acyl or N-alkyl variation of the amide cap; the amide nitrogen only ever sees ethyl, methyl or aryl
no polar neutral substituent to offset mean cLogP 4.34; hydroxyl appears on 28 of 870 and acid on none
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards keeping the N-ethyl-N-(halopyridyl) amide on a fused tricyclic indole and then closing one more ring across it. The top 30 average 4.8 rings and 3.53 bridged ring-pairs against 3.45 and 0.71 for the whole set, and 90% of them contain an aromatic atom shared into a non-aromatic ring; hydrogen-bond donors fall from 1.88 to 0.30 and SA score rises from 3.44 to 4.71. Within that cage the last fifty evaluations only swap F, Cl, Br and methyl: 0.5021 is reached three times by three such variants. Low scores are not wrong chemistry but absent chemistry - the zero-scoring entries are one- and two-atom fragments.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set of the five: mean 47.9 heavy atoms, 697 Da, 6.33 rings of which 5.92 are aromatic, 8.0 rotatable bonds, TPSA 134, QED 0.20, SA 4.57, and 32.6% of proposals above 50 heavy atoms with a maximum of 119. Fluorine dominates (mean 3.55 F per molecule) and it is often not on carbon: N-F in 28.4% of proposals, O-F in 23.7%, and an N,N-difluoroamine in 13.3%. The two sessions that inflate produce visibly repeated fragments strung together by fluorinated amine and urea linkers. Scores occupy a narrow band - digest worst 0.5 (methane scores 0.5), median 0.5885, best 0.6211.
liabilities: O-F hypofluorite bonds in 96.7% of the 30 highest-scoring molecules, a group that cannot be made or handled
N,N-difluoroamine and N-fluoro urea chains in 13.3% of proposals, concentrated in the session that inflates to 119 heavy atoms
molecular weight mean 697 Da with QED 0.20; one third of proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms
visibly duplicated fragments within one molecule, i.e. growth by copying rather than by design
benzylic bromide in 33.3% of the top 30
missing_features: no carbon-bound fluorinated group: trifluoromethyl in 0 of 870, so every fluorine the leaders add is a single F or an F on a heteroatom
nitrile almost absent (6 of 870) where the Parent emitted it in 28.5% of its proposals on the same objective
no compact saturated ring or linker to carry substituents; ring growth is aromatic fusion only (5.92 aromatic of 6.33 rings)
no basic amine (26 of 870) and no charged species of any kind
no mechanism for shrinking: mean size rises across the budget in two of three sessions while the highest scores sit near 28 heavy atoms
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks a fluorine- and chlorine-rich bis-heteroaryl amine with almost no oxygen. The top 30 average 4.07 F and 1.00 Cl against 0.37 and 0.10 for the bottom 30, cLogP 4.77 against 2.27, oxygen count 1.23 against 4.03 - and 96.7% of them carry an O-F bond, up from 23.7% over the whole set. The leaders are also much smaller than the population (28.5 against 47.9 heavy atoms), so the growth the generator spends most of its budget on is not what the score rewards. The Parent reached 0.8561 on the matching seed with 28-31-heavy-atom molecules of the same O-F class, so the ceiling here is a search outcome, not an absence of that chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventionally drug-like set and the only one that saturates: mean 32.2 heavy atoms, 497 Da, 3.5 rings of which 2.17 are aromatic, 8.5 rotatable bonds, cLogP 5.16, TPSA 61, QED 0.37, SA 4.18. A basic secondary or tertiary amine is present in 796 of 870 proposals (91.5%) and in all of the top 30; an aryl halide in 98.4%. The leaders are two-aryl amines around a tetrahydroisoquinoline-like or open aminomethyl core, carrying a phenol, a methoxy and a cyclopropane. Scores run 0.000167 to 0.99998 with digest median 0.6537.
liabilities: beta-chloroamine in 63.3% of the top 30, a nitrogen-mustard-type arrangement that is a hard reject in a real series
free aromatic thiol in 30.7% of all proposals and 16.7% of the top 30
cyclopropane and aziridine rings carrying the key substituent in two thirds of the top 30
mean cLogP 5.16 with 1.58 chlorine atoms per molecule, i.e. the score is reached partly by lipophilicity
the basic nitrogen sits on an open chain in more than half the top 30 (ring amine in 46.7% of them) at a mean 8.57 rotatable bonds, so the leaders are conformationally floppy
missing_features: no unstrained saturated N-heterocycle to carry the basic centre: piperazine ring in 2 of 870 and morpholine in 0, with the basic nitrogen usually acyclic or in a fused ring
no specified configuration at the benzylic amine centre, although 97.9% of proposals contain at least one unassigned stereocentre
no protonated form ever written, so the ionization state the objective implicitly rewards is never represented
no trifluoromethyl or nitrile to tune the aryl rings (0 and 3 of 870)
no ring-closure move that would convert the long acyclic amine chains (mean 8.5 rotatable bonds) into the rigid amine scaffolds the top molecules approximate
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards exactly what the pharmacophore implies and the generator can already build: a basic N-methyl amine two to three bonds from a lipophilic aryl, a second substituted aryl, and low polarity. Top 30 against bottom 30: basic amine 100% against 6.7%, TPSA 48 against 73, cLogP 4.99 against 2.96, phenol 63.3% against 3.3%. The polar groups inherited from the seeded starting molecules are discriminated against and disappear - sulfonyl 24.1% of proposals but 0% of the top 30, carboxylic acid 9.7% but 0%. What rides along with the win is a chloroalkyl group: beta-chloroamine 63.3% and a three-membered carbocycle 66.7% of the top 30, against 27.1% and 13.0% over the whole set.

per_task.generated_character: Large, polar, poly-ring amides with very little halogen - digest halogen_rate 0.194, the lowest of the five. Mean 35.7 heavy atoms, 489 Da, 5.1 rings of which 3.05 are aromatic, cLogP 3.61, TPSA 88.5, QED 0.47, SA 4.32. Amide in 85.7% of proposals and an ether in 87.4%; a diamine ring of the piperazine type in 47.8% overall and 96.7% of the top 30. The leaders are tricyclic pyrazolo-lactams bearing an ortho-ethoxyphenyl and a small strained ring, or quinoline-oxymethyl lactams bearing a methylated diamine ring. The whole score range is compressed: 0.0121 to 0.2434, digest median 0.1916.
liabilities: aziridine and epoxide rings appended directly to an arene in two thirds of the top 30, both reactive alkylators
ketene-type C=C=O arrangements in 3.4% of proposals, including among the final-evaluation molecules
aminal and N-N amide arrangements inside the lactam rings of the leaders
mean 5.1 rings at 489 Da with SA 4.32, so the series is heavy for the activity it reaches
a 0.115-scoring proposal that is two full copies of the same xanthine-amide unit joined by an ester linker
missing_features: no halogen or trifluoromethyl on the aromatic rings of the leaders (0 F, Cl, Br in all 30 top molecules)
no ordinary small saturated substituent in place of the strained rings the search keeps appending
no carboxylic acid, sulfonamide or other anionic or strongly polar handle (acid in 2 of 870, sulfonyl in 3)
no stereochemistry written at any of the ring-junction centres, although 71.3% of proposals carry unassigned centres
no move that merges the two halves into a single compact scaffold; molecules grow by linking pharmacophores through ethers and amides
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards a mid-sized, less polar, two-pharmacophore molecule and punishes accumulation. Top 30 against bottom 30: 35.9 against 43.1 heavy atoms, TPSA 78.8 against 132, HBD 0.67 against 2.07, QED 0.47 against 0.29, and no halogen at all in the top 30 against 0.43 per molecule in the bottom 30. Inside the top the differences are a single appended three-membered ring: aziridine in 40% and epoxide in 26.7% of the top 30 against 3.6% and 4.0% over the whole set, and the 0.2434, 0.2381 and 0.2359 molecules differ only in whether that ring is aziridine, cyclopropane or a four-membered N,O ring. No session exceeds 0.2434, so the gradient is shallow everywhere.

per_task.generated_character: Small, heavily fluorinated, partly dearomatized heterocycles: mean 26.6 heavy atoms, 380 Da, 2.57 rings of which 2.12 are aromatic, cLogP 2.03, TPSA 77, QED 0.53, SA 4.29, and mean 2.54 fluorine atoms per molecule. The fluorine is overwhelmingly on nitrogen: N-F in 67.8% of the 870 proposals and 96.7% of the top 30. The recurring body is a methylated xanthine- or triazinone-like ring bearing an N-fluoro imide, a fluoroalkenyl chain and a fluoromethyl ester. Scores span 5.9e-66 to 0.6618 with digest median 0.3296.
liabilities: N-fluoro amide and N-fluoro imide bonds in 96.7% of the top 30, which are electrophilic fluorinating agents rather than stable substituents
fluoromethyl esters and formate esters (O-CH2F in 36.7% of the top 30), both hydrolytically and metabolically unstable
polyfluorinated acyclic dienes and vinyl fluorides in 63.3% of the top 30
the single best molecule has no aromatic ring at all and an exocyclic C=N amidine on a fluorinated ring, SA 5.1
methane and difluorine still appear as scored proposals (1.6% of proposals below 10 heavy atoms)
missing_features: trifluoromethyl in only 2 of 870 proposals, so the carbon-bound fluorine that this fluorine-hungry gradient would reward is effectively unreachable
no primary or secondary aliphatic amine on a saturated ring (piperidine in 1 of 870, piperazine in 0) despite 43.3% of the top 30 carrying some basic centre
no amide-to-amine or ring-saturation move: the leaders stay imides and enamines rather than becoming saturated amino heterocycles
no stereocentre is ever specified, although 36.7% of proposals have unassigned centres and the top 30 average 1.5 each
no fused bicyclic saturated scaffold; ring count falls to 2.33 in the top 30 with 0.80 bridged pairs instead
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards fluorine count and a specific dearomatized imide ring, and it reaches that by fluorinating heteroatoms rather than carbon. Top 30 against the whole set: 3.97 against 2.54 fluorines, N-F 96.7% against 67.8%, vinyl fluoride 63.3% against 26.4%, O-CH2F 36.7% against 11.6% - while aromatic rings fall from 2.12 to 1.13 and SA score rises from 4.29 to 5.31. A basic amine appears in only 6.7% of proposals but 43.3% of the top 30, so the gradient does ask for a basic centre and the generator supplies it rarely. The two molecules in the whole set that carry a trifluoromethyl score 0.4044 and 0.4006, well below their own session best of 0.5955, so the carbon-bound fluorinated group was found once, late, on an otherwise weak body and was not pursued.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over the 4350 optimizer proposals of this node (3 search seeds, 5 objectives, 300 evaluations each; all fifteen trajectory files read), 1179 (27.1%) contain an N-X, O-X or S-X bond. On one objective 96.7% of the 30 highest-scoring molecules carry an O-F bond and on another 96.7% carry an N-F bond, against set-wide rates of 23.7% and 67.8%. Three proposals are nothing but two bonded halogens, one of which was scored 0.0. The paired code-parent shows 1032 of 4350 on the same seeds, so this is an inherited property, not a new one.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator attaches halogens to heteroatoms as readily as to carbon, and that bond type then dominates its own highest-scoring output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen placement should be restricted to carbon unless the specific heteroatom-halogen environment belongs to a recognized stable class, and the generator needs carbon-bound substitutes that deliver the same electron withdrawal so that removing the unstable bond does not remove the gradient the search was following.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4350 proposals: trifluoromethyl in 2, nitrile in 11, tetrazole in 0, carboxylic acid in 87, and the 213 sulfonyl-bearing molecules are almost entirely descendants of one seeded starting structure. Every observed variation is one atom at a time - F for Cl for Br, methyl for ethyl. The two trifluoromethyl molecules that did appear scored 0.4044 and 0.4006 against a session best of 0.5955 and were not pursued.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot place a multi-atom functional group as one move, so whole classes of common substituents never appear.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add group-level insertion and replacement moves over a fixed library of common substituents, so a multi-atom group can be reached in one accepted step rather than through intermediate structures that each have to survive scoring on their own.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4350 proposals, morpholine appears in 2, an unfused piperazine ring in 15 and piperidine in 114. Meanwhile three-membered rings appear in 66.7% of the top 30 on one objective and aziridine plus epoxide in 66.7% of the top 30 on another, against set-wide rates of 13.0%, 3.6% and 4.0%. On a third objective bridged ring-pairs rise from 0.71 over all proposals to 3.53 in the top 30, with 90% of those leaders sharing an aromatic atom into a non-aromatic ring and SA score rising from 3.44 to 4.71.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction produces strained small rings and bridges across aromatic systems instead of the saturated heterocycles and fused systems that dominate real series.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring-forming moves need to be size- and geometry-aware: offer common saturated and fused ring closures as first-class alternatives, and treat a bridge thrown across an aromatic ring or a strained ring fused to a scoring pharmacophore as a distinct, rarely chosen move rather than the cheapest way to add a ring.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective the mean proposal is 47.9 heavy atoms and 697 Da with QED 0.20, 32.6% of proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest is 119, while the 30 highest-scoring molecules of the same objective average only 28.5 heavy atoms. In one session mean size climbs 44.8, 62.7, 56.6, 64.9, 70.6 across the five fifths of the budget; the paired code-parent stays at 31.4 to 35.6 on the same seed and has 2.3% of proposals above 50 heavy atoms. The largest molecules visibly repeat one fragment inside themselves.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size has no downward pressure; in some sessions the generator grows monotonically and by copying.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Deletion and replacement moves must be as available and as frequently chosen as addition, and duplicated substructure within one candidate should be recognized so that growth is not the default way to explore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4350 proposals carries a stereo designation or a formal charge, while 2282 of them (52.5%) contain at least one unassigned stereocentre; on one objective 97.9% of proposals have an unassigned centre and the 30 best average 3.3 each, and 796 of 870 proposals on that same objective carry a basic amine that would be protonated at physiological pH. This repeats a gap first recorded for the earlier exchange-free count-GP ancestry and re-observed in the code-parent under the same profile and three search seeds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no stereochemistry and no ionization state, even where its own leaders depend on both.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration should be written where the molecule is genuinely stereogenic and resolved or marked otherwise, and the protonation state should be represented explicitly, so that two candidates that differ only in configuration or charge are distinguishable to everything downstream.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Beta-chloroamine appears in 63.3% of the top 30 on one objective against 27.1% of its 870 proposals; benzylic bromide in 23.3% and 33.3% of the top 30 on two others against 8.0% and 4.3% set-wide; a free aromatic thiol in 30.7% of one objective's proposals against 2.3% for the paired code-parent on the same seeds. Each of these sits on the part of the molecule the gradient is rewarding.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive alkylating attachments are not merely tolerated but are enriched in the highest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs non-alkylating replacements that preserve the steric and electronic role of the group it is swapping out, so that an alert-bearing attachment can be exchanged without losing the local environment the surrogate has learned to favour.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Within one objective's twelve best molecules, ten share one scaffold and differ only in CH2Br against CH2F against methyl and Cl against F on the terminal ring, producing three distinct scores across six molecules; on another, the three best differ only in whether one appended three-membered ring is aziridine, cyclopropane or a four-membered N,O ring. Murcko scaffold mode share within the top 50 of a session ranges 0.08 to 0.80 with a mean near 0.40, while every one of the 290 proposals per session is a distinct SMILES.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late-stage exploration collapses to terminal single-atom swaps, so the final budget buys near-duplicates.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep a scaffold-level move available late in the budget, and measure proposal novelty against the incumbent by scaffold rather than by string identity, so that uniqueness counts do not conceal a search that has stopped moving.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local chronological archive, greedy 64-member survivor population and score-quantile parent sampling (edges 0.10/0.25/0.50, weights 0.60/0.30/0.10).

Connected-fragment crossover (p 0.45) with optional finishing mutation (p 0.35) and ordinary one-to-three-call mutation continuation over seven atom/bond/ring families; direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled.
Stable canonical isomeric identity admission with initial/emitted and pool duplicate rejection, max 120 atoms, 160-member fresh de novo pools and announced batches of ten.
Source-relative per-signature sulfur introduction gate over actual scored generating parents.

Count-Morgan (radius 2, 2048 bins, chiral) dot-product generalized-Tanimoto GP term with raw mean/population-SD normalization (floor 0.001), noise SD 0.05, unit prior amplitude, inherited jitter ladder and numerical fallback routing, now the (1-w) term of the covariance.

New: per-refit exact-marginal-likelihood-selected 17-feature whole-molecule composition/property Gaussian kernel channel (w in {0,0.125,0.25,0.5}, l2 in {4.25,17}, archive-standardized with floor 1.0) used coherently in posterior mean and residual covariance.
Correlated joint posterior Thompson allocation: one standard-normal array per batch, sequential availability masks and first-index ties.
